chunks: And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man against whom three men testified that he had committed adultery with a certain woman, and the fourth testified that he did not know with whom he had committed adultery. He said: “He is not to be given the hadd punishment, nor is he to be stoned.”

And he was asked about a muḥṣanah woman who committed adultery while she was pregnant. He said: “She is to be left until she gives birth to what is in her womb and nurses her child, then she is to be stoned.”

key_terms.لَا يُحَدُّ: the hadd punishment is not carried out
key_terms.مُحْصَنَةٍ: a married woman under the legal status of iḥṣān

ai.seo_question: What happens in Islamic law if four witnesses do not fully agree in a zinā case, and what is the ruling for a pregnant married woman who committed adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings related to zinā, emphasizing the strict evidentiary standard required for implementing the hadd or rajm. It also states that a pregnant muḥṣanah is not punished immediately; her punishment is delayed until after childbirth and nursing, preserving the life and welfare of the child.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5035 - It is narrated from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati that Abu Abdullah (as) said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man against whom three men testified that he had committed adultery with a certain woman, but the fourth witness testified that he did not know with whom the man had committed adultery.
Imam (as) replied: "He is neither to be punished with lashes nor stoned."

Imam (as) was also asked about a married woman who committed adultery and was pregnant. Imam (as) said: "She should be kept until she gives birth to what is in her womb and nurses her child, then she is to be stoned."
